Church_of_St_Janyl.prompt: Wide news photograph taken from the crowded esplanade below Cathedral Hill on the feast of St. Janyl in late August, 24mm lens, hazy morning light. A great 18th-century Central Asian cathedral crowns the hilltop: built of plain warm yellow fired brick laid in decorative patterns, like the Timurid and Kokand brick monuments of Turkestan but a Christian church, a massive cross-shaped body with tall pointed-arch portals framed in carved walnut, rising to one huge ribbed dome clad in faded turquoise glazed tiles on a tall sixteen-windowed octagonal drum, crowned by an iron cross with flared equal arms. Old brick monastery walls and cloisters wrap around the hill, broad stone stairs climb up to the cathedral. Tens of thousands of pilgrims pack the esplanade and the stairs, women in white headscarves, old men in tall white felt hats with black brims, horsemen, priests in black cassocks and tall black hats, flocks of sheep being blessed, blue juniper smoke. Dry brown foothills behind. Real documentary photograph, natural colours.
